title: Arrays from Zero to Hero
description: A guided course that takes a learner from basic array indexing to common interview-grade array techniques, one chapter at a time.

nodes.title: Array Basics
nodes.description: Reading, writing and iterating over arrays.
nodes.theory:
## Arrays

An array stores elements contiguously, so indexing is O(1). In this lesson you'll practice reading and writing elements and iterating with a simple loop.

```python
nums = [4, 8, 15]
for n in nums:
    print(n)
```

**Key takeaways**
- Indexes start at 0.
- Reading by index costs the same for any position.

nodes.title: Walking Through an Array
nodes.description: Visit every element once to count, sum or search.
nodes.theory:
## Iteration

Most array work is a single pass: keep a running value and update it for each element.

```python
total = 0
for n in nums:
    total += n
```

questions.explanation: Indexes start at 0, so nums[1] is the second element.

questions.prompt: Reading an element by its index takes the same time for any index.
questions.explanation: Indexing is O(1): the position is computed directly.

questions.prompt: Complete the loop so it adds up every number.
questions.explanation: `for n in nums` visits each element and `+=` adds it to the total.

questions.prompt: This code should print the last element. Which line is wrong?
questions.explanation: The last index is len(nums) - 1; nums[len(nums)] is out of range.

nodes.title: The Two-Pointer Technique
nodes.description: Solve array problems in a single pass using two indices.
nodes.theory:
## Two pointers

Many array problems that look like they need O(n^2) can be solved in O(n) by walking two indices toward each other or in the same direction.

questions.prompt: Put the lines in order so the function reverses the list in place.
questions.explanation: Start with both pointers at the ends, then swap and move them toward each other until they meet.

questions.prompt: The two-pointer technique always needs the array to be sorted.
questions.explanation: Reversing or partitioning works on any array; only pair-sum style searches rely on sorting.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of reversing a list with two pointers?
questions.explanation: Each element is swapped at most once, so the pass is linear.
